title: DEFINE delta detection and freeze record foundation
description: rcf-lite gains three pure primitives and one durable record. hashDocument returns a sha256:<hex> hash over the canonical JSON of a parsed document (keys sorted recursively, no whitespace). computeTreeHash hashes the sorted (id, docHash) pairs. computeDelta(tree, freeze, ledgers) returns the whole change model of the proposal (2026-09-22 v3) section 2.2: frozen, frozenAt, treeHash, currentTreeHash, changed, added, removed, briefSince, unchanged. docHashes cover every standalone document the walker exposes on tree.byId (PRD, TAD, BS, REQ, US, TAC, ADR, FBS, TS, CN, EVAL) plus one ledger:<name> entry per sidecar the caller passes in. Before the first freeze the delta is the whole tree (frozen false, everything in added). The freeze record itself sits at rcf/define/freeze.json (owned by rcf-lite, outside the shared rcf-schemas package until 0.7) with a small local schema and a reader/writer module: reading a missing file returns null, a malformed file raises a clear error. No rcf define freeze verb yet; the writer the verb will call is exposed for slice 3.
rationale: Barry's backstory dogfood found DEFINE generated too fast with no gates. Baz ruled 2026-09-22 that the fix is detection over configured change records: the freeze remembers what the tree looked like; anything that differs is the change. The delta.js primitives are what every later slice (gates, readiness, freeze verb, bundle read, viewer tab) consumes, so their return shape is a contract worth pinning early. Canonical-JSON hashing (over raw bytes) is the difference between a real change and a hand reformat; document granularity (over criterion granularity) keeps the model cheap while git supplies the criterion-level diff.
